The hailstorm completely destroyed Lencho's field. It covered the land with ice and ruined the corn crop. The flowers had been knocked down and the leaves and plants were damaged. The crop looked as if it had been covered by a layer of snow. Lencho was devastated because he had expected a good harvest. He had nothing left from which he could earn money. The destruction made him depend on his faith in God.

Nelson Mandela struggled against apartheid, the system of racial discrimination that denied black people their basic rights. He joined the African National Congress and took part in the freedom struggle. He was imprisoned for many years because of his opposition to apartheid. During his imprisonment he remained committed to equality and justice. He later helped negotiate the end of apartheid. In 1994 South Africa held its first democratic elections based on universal adult suffrage. Mandela became the country's first black President. His struggle helped establish a democratic and non-racial South Africa.

The incident in 'Dust of Snow' appears negative because a crow and a hemlock tree are normally associated with unpleasant images. Yet the crow shakes snow onto the poet and changes his mood. The small experience removes his sadness and regret. It makes him feel that a part of the day has been saved. The poem therefore shows that even an unexpected or unpleasant-looking event can have a positive effect. A change in perspective can bring hope. Thus a negative-looking moment can produce a positive emotional result.

The poet uses humour, rhyme and exaggeration to distinguish wild animals. The lion is recognised by its roar, the tiger by its dangerous attack, the leopard by its leap and the bear by its hug. The hyena is described through its laugh-like expression and the crocodile through its tears. These clues are playful rather than scientific. The poet makes dangerous animals sound funny and memorable. The humorous descriptions make the poem enjoyable while helping the reader identify the animals.

Coorg is called a piece of heaven because of its beautiful geographical features. It is situated between Mysore and Mangalore and is surrounded by hills and forests. The region has evergreen forests, coffee plantations and cardamom-growing areas. The Brahmagiri hills add to its scenic beauty. The river Kaveri rises in the hills of Coorg. The cool climate, misty hills and rich greenery make the landscape attractive. Its natural beauty and biodiversity make Coorg a wonderful place to visit. OR Buddha teaches that life is marked by suffering because birth, old age, illness and death are unavoidable. Kisa Gotami learns that death is common to all when she searches for a house untouched by death. Buddha explains that attachment to worldly things causes sorrow. A wise person understands the impermanent nature of life. One should not remain trapped in grief over what cannot be changed. Acceptance and detachment help a person attain peace. The lesson therefore teaches compassion, understanding and freedom from excessive attachment.

The poem 'The Trees' presents a conflict between human control and the natural desire for freedom. The trees are imagined as being trapped inside a house. Their branches and roots struggle to escape towards the forest and the open sky. Human beings have confined nature within walls and made it decorative or controlled. The trees, however, continue to move towards their natural home. The poet suggests that nature cannot be permanently imprisoned. The movement of the trees symbolises the restoration of freedom. Thus the poem highlights the conflict between human interference and nature's independent life. OR It is not right to judge a person only by physical appearance. In 'For Anne Gregory', the young woman's beautiful hair attracts human beings, but the poem questions whether such attraction is genuine love. Physical beauty can change through age or even through something as simple as hair dye. Human beings may be attracted by outward appearance, while true love should recognise the inner self. The poem says that only God can love a person for the self alone. Therefore, character and inner qualities are more important than appearance. We should respect people for who they are rather than for how they look.

Ban Plastics – Save Environment: Plastic is convenient, but excessive use of it has become a serious environmental problem. Plastic bags and other single-use items often remain in the environment for many years. They pollute streets, rivers, lakes and oceans. Animals may swallow plastic or become trapped in it. Burning plastic can also release harmful substances. We should reduce the use of single-use plastic products. Cloth and reusable bags can replace plastic carry bags. Bottles and containers should be reused whenever possible. Waste should be separated so that recyclable plastic can be processed properly. Schools can teach students about the dangers of plastic pollution. Shops and consumers should support eco-friendly alternatives. Governments should enforce rules against unnecessary single-use plastics. Communities must prevent plastic from entering drains and water bodies. Every person can make a difference through small daily choices. A cleaner environment means healthier lives for people and animals. Therefore, banning or reducing unnecessary plastic is an important step towards saving the environment. Public awareness and responsible habits are equally important. Every reduction in unnecessary plastic use is a step towards a cleaner future. OR Manners Maketh a Man: Good manners are an important part of a person's character. They teach us to respect others and behave thoughtfully. Simple words such as please, thank you and sorry can make communication pleasant. Good manners include speaking politely, listening patiently and helping people when possible. They also mean respecting elders, teachers, workers and people from every background. A well-mannered person does not insult others or behave arrogantly. Manners help create harmony at home, at school and in society. They are especially important when people disagree. Good manners do not mean weakness; they show self-control and maturity. Students should practise courtesy in classrooms and public places. They should also respect queues, public property and other people's time. Modern life becomes easier when people treat one another with consideration. Education is incomplete without good behaviour. A person's achievements are more valuable when accompanied by kindness and respect. Therefore, good manners truly help make a person worthy and respected. Courtesy costs nothing but creates trust and goodwill. Therefore, good manners should be practised throughout life.
